best_for: Windows and Mac users who want ads and trackers blocked in every app, not just the browser, and who will pay for a license after the trial.

points.title: Filters every app, not just the browser
points.text: AdGuard installs a network driver and filters the traffic of all programs on the computer. Browser extensions only see the browser.

points.title: HTTPS filtering means a root certificate
points.text: To clean encrypted pages, AdGuard decrypts them on your machine with its own root certificate added to the system. Uninstalling it removes those changes.

points.title: DNS and parental controls
points.text: It can block requests to known ad and tracking servers at the DNS level and encrypt your DNS traffic. Parental controls hide adult sites in search and support custom blocklists.

points.title: Paid after 14 days
points.text: The Windows and Mac apps come with a 14-day trial. After that you need a license: Personal covers 3 devices and Family covers 9, each as a yearly plan or a one-time Lifetime purchase. One license works across Windows, Mac and Android.

points.title: Windows 10 or later
points.text: AdGuard 8 dropped Windows 8 and 8.1. The stated minimum is Windows 10 with 6 GB of RAM, a 2 GHz dual-core processor and 4 GB of free disk. Older systems can use an older version, which no longer gets updates.

points.title: Mac needs macOS 12
points.text: The Mac app is a universal download for Intel and Apple silicon and needs macOS 12 or later. The Windows installer installs for the whole machine.

points.title: Older versions on Windows only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 41 versions. macOS lists only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
